links.outcome: Presence of structured monitoring of deployed AI for degradation and drift in institutions
links.effect: Participants recognized that AI models degrade over time from data drift, practice changes and poor generalizability, but monitoring practices remain ad hoc and fragmented, with few institutions investing in structured oversight infrastructure.
links.quote: However, monitoring practices remain ad hoc and fragmented, with few institutions investing in structured oversight infrastructure.

links.outcome: Clarity of responsibility for AI maintenance and monitoring tasks
links.effect: Maintenance and monitoring tasks were described as poorly defined, inconsistently performed, and undervalued across healthcare systems, a 'responsibility vacuum'.
links.quote: This study explores the phenomenon of a "responsibility vacuum" in AI governance, wherein maintenance and monitoring tasks are poorly defined, inconsistently performed, and undervalued across healthcare systems.

screen.reason: Qualitative interview study examining the real-world deployment challenges and governance/monitoring practices of AI in healthcare systems.
